text:
clare (Finance): AlpenCloud sent invoice AC-2026-900 for CHF 63,200. Invoice header: 'AlpenCloud AG (CH) — UK branch billing'. They charged 20% UK VAT on top and inserted a 'gross-up for withholding & experiment delta' clause. Also attached a CSV 'usage_adjustments.csv' showing a +12% line-item labeled 'pricing experiment delta'. Can we pay as-is?
harry (AP): Whoa. Mixed-country header + VAT charged = red flag. Do we have PO? PO 49800 matches amount. Uploaded PDF + CSV to drive: https://drive.redwood/alpencloud/AC-2026-900.pdf & https://drive.redwood/alpencloud/usage_adjustments.csv
billing-bot: PO 49800 matched. Payment blocked: tax mismatch + non-standard contract clause.
eva (Tax): Quick checklist: 1) If billed by UK-registered branch, invoice needs a valid UK VAT registration number. 2) If billed by Swiss parent (CH), they should not charge UK VAT; reverse charge or no VAT depending on place of supply. Switzerland is non-EU so VIES won't help. Need clear proof (UK VAT cert or CH UID and place-of-supply rationale). 3) Gross-up + pricing-experiment charge is commercial — tax team can't approve that without docs.
mike (Legal): We do not accept unilateral gross-up clauses by default. Also any retrospective charge arising from a vendor pricing experiment needs commercial approval. Ask them to remove the clause and provide explanation + legal entity confirmation.
clare (Finance): Action items: ask vendor to (A) reissue invoice from the correct legal entity with matching tax id, (B) remove the gross-up clause, (C) provide a breakdown of the 'pricing experiment delta' with original contract reference, and (D) supply either UK VAT cert if UK branch or CH UID + place-of-supply analysis if Swiss parent.
harry (AP): Also request proof that the +12% is agreed in writing (email/ammendment). Until we have that payment stays on hold.
alpencloud (vendor): Hi Redwood — we rolled out a VAT handling change during a billing experiment in Jan and some accounts were billed via our UK branch for customer convenience. The delta is due to switching SKU mappings. We'll attach a reconciliation and UK VAT number for the branch. We flagged gross-up because our tax team wanted protection in case of withholding.
eva (Tax): Ok if they provide a valid UK VAT number that matches the invoicing entity and attach the VAT registration screenshot/confirmation (or a VAT certificate), we can accept VAT. If they claim Swiss parent issued invoice then VAT should be removed and reverse charge considered.
mike (Legal): Vendor note: decline gross-up clause. We can accept a commercial request for retroactive adjustments but it needs procurement sign-off + a written amendment. Don't let them tie it to tax indemnity.
clare (Finance): Vendor attached: (1) UK VAT number GB999888777, (2) a two-page reconciliation PDF, (3) email thread showing 'pricing experiment' approval by their sales ops (screenshot).
harry (AP): Running quick checks: HMRC VAT check for GB999888777 returns valid? (someone run the HMRC VAT checker).
eva (Tax): If HMRC confirms, AP can accept VAT charges. But we still need to review reconciliation CSV to ensure the delta isn't a rebilling that should have been credited earlier. If it's truly retroactive, Procurement chargeback required.
alpencloud (vendor): We can reissue corrected invoice without the gross-up clause and include a separate credit note for the portion disputed if Redwood prefers.
clare (Finance): Preferred: reissue one clean invoice (matching entity + UK VAT cert) and issue a separate credit/adj for experiment-related differences if any. That keeps VAT accounting clean. Also ask them to confirm no withholding issues — gross-up removed.
harry (AP): I'll keep payment on hold. Once reissued invoice + UK VAT evidence + reconciliation are in Drive and AP verifies PO match and credit note if needed, I'll release.
mike (Legal): If vendor pushes for indemnity or automatic gross-up, escalate to Procurement & Legal for contract amendment.
eva (Tax): Final: Tax will sign off if documentation matches: legal entity matches VAT id, HMRC check OK, and pricing delta is supported by reconciliation/contract note. If any withholding claim arises, we'll need TRC/evidence; but Swiss/UK mix usually doesn't create withholding for payments of service fees.
clare (Finance): Thanks team. I'll request reissue and reconcilation now and follow up in 48 hours. :thumbsup:
billing-bot: Invoice AC-2026-900 flagged as 'on hold - tax documentation requested' and will be reviewed after new docs uploaded.
clare (Finance): Marking thread resolved for now — will reopen if vendor reintroduces gross-up. :white_check_mark:
